vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: tickerdb
Version: 0.1.4

The tickerdb skill is a legitimate market intelligence integration for the TickerDB.com API. It implements a transparent authentication flow (email verification) and utilizes standard OpenClaw features like 'config set' for API key management and 'cron add' for scheduled market reports. No evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or prompt injection was found in SKILL.md or _meta.json.

llm.summary: The skill is internally consistent with its stated purpose — it only requires a TICKERDB_KEY and its runtime instructions focus on calling the TickerDB API — but it will collect a user email and an API key during onboarding and offers to persist that key, so users should be aware of credential persistence.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (query TickerDB for categorical market intelligence) matches the declared requirement (TICKERDB_KEY) and the SKILL.md which documents API endpoints and asset rules. No unrelated credentials, binaries, or installs are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md stays within the skill's scope: it describes authentication, summary/search/watchlist API calls, and onboarding questions. It instructs the agent to collect the user's email and 2-step verification code to obtain an API key and to call GET/POST endpoints on api.tickerdb.com. This is expected, but the onboarding explicitly asks the agent to display and (optionally) persist the returned apiKey — users should be aware the agent will handle credentials and email addresses.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec and no code files. Lowest-risk install profile (nothing is downloaded or written by the skill itself).
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only one environment variable (TICKERDB_KEY) is required and declared as the primary credential. That is proportional to a service API integration and matches the documented Authorization header usage.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and no elevated system persistence are requested. However, the onboarding flow instructs the agent to obtain an apiKey and offers to save it; the SKILL.md notes 'OpenClaw persists it automatically' when the user confirms. This is normal for API-key-based skills but is an important privacy/credential-persistence behavior to surface to end users.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: it queries TickerDB and only needs a TICKERDB_KEY. Before installing or enabling it, confirm you trust tickerdb.com and are comfortable giving the agent your email to complete login and handing it an API key. When the skill offers to save the apiKey, decline if you do not want it persisted by the platform. Prefer creating a least-privilege API key on TickerDB (if the site supports key scopes or expirations). Do not reuse unrelated service credentials. If you plan to allow autonomous agent runs, remember the agent could query the service using the stored key when invoked.
